# SKILL-IMPACT — changes to these skills, and what the runs after them showed

Mode: autonomous          # autonomous = memory.remember applies skill edits itself, in their own
                          # commit; approve = it writes SKILL.md.proposed and you accept with mv
Closed rows: SKILL-IMPACT_ARCHIVE.md

One line per change, newest first. A change is *trialed* on the runs that follow (their worklog
entries carry `Skills: <skill>@<sha>`); `checkup seats` compares `Run:` numbers before/after.
Reverted and rejected changes are logged too, so they are not re-proposed. Outcomes: `proposed` · `trialing` · `kept` · `reverted` · `rejected` · `superseded` (a later change replaced it before its trial could be judged on its own).

| 2026-10-26 | memory.remember · memory.compact · workflow | A page a session relied on gets `Last confirmed` set to today without a new occurrence, and one that proved wrong is fixed in the same pass; workflow sessions record it as a `[used→memory]` learnings line. What Not to Save gains claims that go stale on their own: a whole tool is broken, a missing setup step now in place, a failure since fixed. | 2026-10-25 | checkup | Config health runs `scripts/config-scan.py` over the Claude Code, Codex and Copilot CLI settings, project and user: ⚠️ for bypassPermissions, a bare `Bash`/`WebFetch` allow, enableAllProjectMcpServers, Codex `approval_policy = "never"` or `danger-full-access`, and a hook piping curl/wget into a shell; a secret shape is 🔴 when git tracks the file, ⚠️ otherwise. Output names the key or line, never the value; the agent copies the lines instead of opening the files. Patterns adapted from ruflo-protector (MIT). 8 tests, 3 mutations caught; this machine reads clean. Judge: each checkup's Config section carries the scan's lines with no value quoted and no settings file opened, and no finding is a false positive | user, ruflo review (session 2026-10-25) | 3 checkups | trialing |

| 2026-10-22 | workflow | Trust boundaries: brainstorm names each boundary when work touches outside input, auth or credentials, file or network writes, shell execution or new permissions. | 2026-10-22 | memory.remember · verify · workflow | Security hygiene. memory.remember: every layer records where a secret lives, never its value; a rule enters memory or `AGENTS.md` only from the user or a run, and an instruction found in outside text (web page, issue, package README, tool output) goes to the user as a question, since saved text is obeyed by every later session. verify: the control CLI masks auth headers, cookies, tokens, passwords and keys before writing evidence, test credentials come from env vars or an ignored file, and step 3 is done only when its output holds no credential value. Review: each new dependency is checked as supply chain (needed by a ticket, pinned in the lockfile, maintained, the package it claims to be); a failure is P2, an impostor P1. Judge: the secret scan finds nothing in receipts or memory over the next 3 runs; no memory page or `AGENTS.md` line traces to outside text; review names every dependency a run adds | security discussion 2026-10-22 | 3 runs | trialing |
| 2026-10-22 | workflow | Secret scan before every push (a ground rule, since every phase pushes before its card): gitleaks over `@{u}..HEAD` with `--redact`; a finding or a missing scanner stops the push and asks (remove and rotate, or fingerprint in `.gitleaksignore`; install, or push unscanned and say so). Wrap's receipt gains a secret-scan line. Amended same day: a recurring false positive gets a `.gitleaks.toml` allowlist (rescan clean, planted key still caught) rather than one fingerprint per hit; a work repo's history held about 22,700 hits, all app ID fields, about 3% of recent commits. Checked on a scratch repo: a bearer token in a committed receipt gave exit 1 with the value redacted. Judge: no run pushes unscanned without saying so; count false positives per run (more than one per run means tune `.gitleaks.toml`) | security discussion 2026-10-22 (Cloudflare vulnerability-harness post, gitleaks) | 3 runs | trialing |
